correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the query domain V(T)x{0,1,2}, single target per selected vertex, all 2^|S| response patterns and exactly three labelled colors. Two selected colors at one vertex fail the all-one response. A selected induced P4 forces a contradictory binary pattern, proving the universal P4-free necessary condition. For the (3,2,1)-spider, admissible target sequences on three arms allow labelings that exclude every possible center color; the restriction remains valid for any supertree. For the positive direction ONLY at |V|<=7, a complete independent enumeration generated every nonisomorphic tree of orders 1..7, tested every P4-free subset against all proper colorings and every possible target assignment, finding exactly one exception. It separately yields VC dimension five; no global sufficiency theorem for larger trees is claimed.

value.rationale: The first forbidden branching configuration separates a simple induced-subgraph necessary condition from actual color-query shatterability, with a sharp seven-vertex boundary and a hereditary obstruction. This is a motivated exact structural classification at the smallest nontrivial complexity, not just an arbitrary finite table.

final_claim: For each nonempty tree with at most seven vertices, a set of distinct vertex-equality color queries is shattered by proper labelled 3-colorings iff its induced subgraph is P4-free, except for the unique marked 7-vertex (3,2,1)-spider with all six arm vertices selected. This spider has VC dimension five; any supertree retaining that selected marked spider is obstructed.
